soap_note.subjective: Patient reports pain on the lateral aspect of right elbow for several months, worsening in the last few weeks. Pain is described as aching and sharp at times, with increased severity during wrist flexion and pronation. Patient reports using ibuprofen for temporary relief. No history of trauma or triggers.  Pain does not radiate to other areas. Patient denies numbness, tingling, coldness, or changes in bowel movements, urination, vision, hearing, smell, taste, or energy levels. Denies recent travel or exposure to sick individuals.
soap_note.objective: Tenderness on lateral aspect of right elbow. Mild swelling noted. Full range of motion of both elbow and hand. No redness or deformity observed.
soap_note.assessment: Lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow) is suspected based on the patient's history, symptoms, and examination findings.
soap_note.plan: 1. Activity modification: Avoid repetitive motions involving wrist extension and pronation at work. 2. Compression sleeve application for pain relief. 3. NSAIDs or Tylenol for pain management. 4. Physical therapy to improve mobility and strength in the affected arm. 5. Ice application for pain and swelling as needed.
